name: Pull-up bar

image.credit: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gymnastics rings hung from a doorway pull-up bar 02.jpg
image.caption: Pull-up bar

lead: A pull-up bar is a fixed horizontal bar, mounted in a doorway, on a wall or ceiling, or on a freestanding frame, for pull-ups, chin-ups and hanging core work. It is among the cheapest ways to train the whole back, and people use it to build the wider lats and stronger upper back behind a V-taper, where the waist looks narrower and clothes fit better.

Vertical pulling loads the lats, biceps, lower trapezius and rear shoulder muscles. Electromyography studies of pull-up variations show high lat activity across common grips with modest differences. Research on pull-ups consists mainly of such comparisons rather than trials of physique outcomes.

paras: Users train pull-ups a few times a week and progress by adding reps, weight, slower tempo or harder variations. Beginners who cannot do one yet use bands or lowering reps first. Hangs are used for grip and shoulder work.

Doorway bars can mar trim or fail if installed poorly, and wall-mounted bars need studs or masonry. Elbow and shoulder overuse injuries are common, particularly with kipping or high weekly volume. A 2026 analysis of US emergency department data estimated about 41,000 visits for pull-up bar injuries over ten years.

angle.text: Users do pull-ups and hangs to build back and shoulder width, creating a V-taper that makes the waist look narrower and improves how clothes fit. Vertical pulling loads the lats and upper back, and strong scapular muscles are said to support posture. The V-taper payoff is mostly reported by lifters.

lead: A pull-up bar is a fixed horizontal bar from which the user hangs to perform pull-ups, chin-ups and hanging exercises. Bars are sold for doorway mounting, wall or ceiling mounting, and as freestanding frames. The pull-up is an upper-body strength exercise in which the body is suspended by the hands, usually gripping the bar wider than shoulder width, and pulled up so that the elbows move toward the torso [1].

The exercise loads the latissimus dorsi, trapezius and biceps brachii and is widely used as a measure of upper-body strength, endurance and strength-to-weight ratio [1]. In looksmaxxing discussion, pull-up bars are associated with building back and shoulder width (the "V-taper"), which proponents say makes the waist appear narrower in proportion and improves how clothes fit.

Research on pull-ups consists mainly of electromyography studies comparing variations rather than trials of physique outcomes. A 2010 study compared pull-up and chin-up variations in trained adults [2], and a 2017 study compared traditional, suspension and towel pull-ups [3]. Wikipedia reports that overall muscle activation was similar across grip variants [1]. A 2026 analysis of United States emergency department data estimated about 41,000 visits for pull-up bar injuries over ten years [4].

paras: From a hanging position the body is pulled up vertically and then lowered until the arms and shoulders are fully extended. The top position may be chin over bar or higher [1]. The pull-up is a closed-chain compound movement involving elbow flexion and shoulder adduction or extension [1]. Pull-ups are usually done on a bar, but towels, rotating handles or gymnastics rings can be used [1].

Grips can be pronated, supinated (commonly called a chin-up) or neutral. Wikipedia reports that when participants choose their own grip width it is typically 20 to 50 percent wider than shoulder width, and that a very wide grip could increase injury risk or reduce repetitions by lengthening the lever arm [1].

According to Wikipedia, the trapezius, infraspinatus and brachialis are most active at the start of the movement, the latissimus dorsi, teres major and biceps peak in the middle, and the triceps and subscapularis peak at the top [1]. Wikipedia cites a 2017 study finding that a pronated grip activated the middle trapezius more than a neutral grip, while overall activation across grip variants was similar [1]. Because activation differences between common grips are modest, improvements are generally attributed to progressive overload, such as more repetitions, added load or slower tempo, as in other resistance training.

Pull-ups are described as correlated with job-related tasks in firefighting, policing and military roles and as a conditioning activity for climbing, gymnastics, rowing and swimming [1]. Many beginners cannot perform an unassisted pull-up; Wikipedia cites a 2003 study in college-age women in which one third completed a pull-up after a twelve-week full-body strength programme [1].

No trial identified examined whether a pull-up bar changes back width or visual proportions. The general claim that vertical pulling builds back muscle rests on resistance-training principles and on electromyography showing high lat activity across common variations [2][3].

A 2026 analysis of the US Consumer Product Safety Commission's NEISS data from 2015 to 2024 estimated about 40,987 emergency department visits attributed to pull-up bar injuries, around 4,000 a year, with a peak of 5,421 in 2024. Patients were predominantly male (66.1 percent) with peaks among children aged 5 to 14 and adults aged 18 to 34, and head and facial injuries accounted for nearly half of presentations [4].

Wikipedia notes that overhead movements such as pull-ups narrow the subacromial space and carry a risk of shoulder impingement, and cites one study in which a pronated shoulder-width grip carried less impingement risk than other variations studied [1]. A case report described palmar calluses, termed pull-up palms, in a man who had performed pull-ups for several years [5]. Doorway bars and wall mounts also carry installation and load-rating considerations.

No trials were found of pull-up bars for appearance outcomes. Related studies include electromyographic comparisons of pull-up and chin-up variations in trained adults [2] and of traditional, suspension-device and towel pull-ups [3]. A crossover study of whole-body vibration before a static pull-up bar hang measured forearm muscle activity in 15 men [6]. A study of assisted jumping used a resistance band attached to a pull-up bar [7]. Injury epidemiology is reported in an emergency department analysis [4] and a case report [5].

Pull-up bars are discussed as one of the cheapest ways to train the back and as a counterpart to pressing exercises for balanced upper-body development, with progress tracked by repetitions or added weight. Threads on bodyweight-fitness forums commonly ask about doorway bars that do not require screws or drilling. Community-specific claims about physique outcomes were limited in the material reviewed.

Product types include tension-mounted doorway bars, doorframe-mounted bars that rest on the frame, wall and ceiling-mounted bars that require anchoring into studs or masonry, and freestanding stations. Considerations commonly discussed are the weight rating, whether installation is damaging to trim, grip positions and ceiling height.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org and T Nation, pull-up bars are discussed as inexpensive home-training equipment, often alongside dumbbells [8][9][10].
